ops.title: Phase D is on: the daemon amortizes derived state, not an embedding engine
ops.body:
Owner decision 2026-07-27, taken against measured numbers rather than the original
argument. Supersedes the daemon rationale in doc `3d9c793`.

## The old justification is dead

The plan justified the daemon by `em_load_model` at 133 ms, 79% of warm embedding
engine init. The dense lane is dropped (note `1a3f9c7`), so there is no engine and
no such cost.

## The measured case that replaces it

Real runs on this repo and `~/Code/monorepo`:

```
kg.Load (bbolt open + digest match), warm     23-34 us
  materialize Index back into a *kg.Graph     7.32 / 8.77 ms
eval.LoadCorpus                               36.9 / 88.1 ms
stale.Assess (+DefaultPolicy)                 738.8 ms / 10.43 s   peak RSS 1.86 GB
rank.New (BM25 index + PPR prior)             11.6 / 19.7 ms
rank.Ranker.Retrieve, warm                    4.31 / 6.10 ms
end-to-end in a fresh process                 857 ms / 4.46-7.45 s
```

`kg.Load` being 23 us is real but irrelevant on its own, for two reasons the
measurement surfaced:

1. **Shape mismatch.** `rank.New` takes a flat `*kg.Graph`; `kg.Index` exposes only
   `Node`/`Out`/`In`/`Events`/`Counts` random access. Feeding the ranker means a
   full-bucket JSON decode.
2. **The index persists only the graph.** The corpus and the staleness assessments
   are rebuilt every process, and `stale.ScanTree` walking the monorepo worktree is
   the single largest cost anywhere in the system.

So residency amortizes *derived state* — materialized graph, BM25 index, PPR prior,
assessments — not model weights.

## The alternative that was rejected

Persisting corpus and assessments under the same source digest and relaxing the hook
budget to ~100 ms lands at 85-93 ms measured today, and deletes Phase D entirely. The
owner chose the 10 ms target and the daemon instead.

## The constraint this runs into

The same measurement found a Go binary costs **~13.7 ms** to spawn (50 sequential
spawns, 0.683 s) against 3.5 ms for `/usr/bin/true`. If that holds for a minimal
binary, **no spawned Go client can meet 10 ms** — process start alone exceeds it.
The plan's "static-binary exec ~5 ms" is in doubt.

The unexplored way out: capt-hook's hooks are Python and that interpreter is already
running when a hook fires, so a Python client pays no exec at all. The cost is
speaking daemonkit's Go framing protocol from Python. This is measured and settled
before any service code is written, not assumed.
